[EarthCam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EarthCam "EarthCam") footage of the collision taken from the [Kennedy Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_Center_for_the_Performing_Arts "John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts"), looking southeast

The two aircraft collided at 8:47:59. The recorded [radio altitude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radar_altimeter "Radar altimeter") of the Black Hawk at the time of the collision was 278 feet (85 m).[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-NTSB2025-02-14-21) The helicopter exploded and both aircraft crashed into the Potomac River. The airliner's airspeed was 128 miles per hour (206 km/h; 111 kn).[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-41) The CRJ700's radio [transponder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transponder_(aeronautics) "Transponder (aeronautics)") ceased transmitting about 2,400 feet (730 m) short of Runway 33.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-AP-3)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-42)

The collision was captured by a webcam at the [John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_Center_for_the_Performing_Arts "John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts"),[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-43)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-44) and another video showed a brief trail of fire.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-45) Other videos showed that the collision may have damaged the rotor blades of the Black Hawk and the left wing of the CRJ700 as the airliner fell in a left-hand spiral into the water.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-46) Witnesses reported that the airliner "split in half" upon impact, while the helicopter crashed upside down near the airliner.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-BBC-47) A pilot in another aircraft confirmed seeing the crash to an air traffic controller and reported seeing flares from the opposite side of the Potomac as his flight was on [short final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final_approach "Final approach").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-Regan-2025-5)

Within three hours of the collision, authorities confirmed fatalities.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-Regan-2025-5)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-WaPo_live-48) By 2:50 a.m. the following morning, no survivors had been reported, and the search and rescue operations were described as "becoming more grim".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-Regan-2025-5) By the afternoon, all 67 people on board both aircraft were presumed dead.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-49)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-50)

It was the first major commercial passenger flight accident in the US in nearly 16 years, following [Colgan Air Flight 3407](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colgan_Air_Flight_3407 "Colgan Air Flight 3407") in February 2009. It was also the first fatal crash involving American Airlines since [Flight 587](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Airlines_Flight_587 "American Airlines Flight 587") in November 2001,[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-51) as well as the first fatal crash of a CRJ700 series aircraft.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-52) It was the first crash in the Potomac River since [Air Florida Flight 90](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Florida_Flight_90 "Air Florida Flight 90") in January 1982.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-53)

### Emergency response

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Emergency response")]

Video 4[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PSA_Airlines_Flight_5342_wreckage_with_skyline_and_runway_for_bearings.webm "Play video")[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PSA_Airlines_Flight_5342_wreckage_with_skyline_and_runway_for_bearings.webm)

[National Transportation Safety Board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Transportation_Safety_Board "National Transportation Safety Board") drone footage, with [Reagan National Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan_Washington_National_Airport "Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport")'s runway 33 in the background

Chief John Donnelly of the [District of Columbia Fire and Emergency Medical Services Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/District_of_Columbia_Fire_and_Emergency_Medical_Services_Department "District of Columbia Fire and Emergency Medical Services Department") (DC FEMS) said emergency responders were notified of an aircraft crash at 8:48 p.m. The first units arrived at the scene at 8:58 p.m., where they discovered the aircraft in the water.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-54) DC FEMS was joined by emergency personnel from the [Metropolitan Police Department of the District of Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Police_Department_of_the_District_of_Columbia "Metropolitan Police Department of the District of Columbia"), [Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority Fire and Rescue Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Washington_Airports_Authority_Fire_and_Rescue_Department "Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority Fire and Rescue Department"), [United States Coast Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Coast_Guard "United States Coast Guard"), [Maryland State Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland_State_Police "Maryland State Police"), along with other local, state, and federal agencies. Additionally, several [Hornblower Cruises](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hornblower_Cruises "Hornblower Cruises") tour boats sailed from the [Washington Sailing Marina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Sailing_Marina "Washington Sailing Marina") in [Alexandria, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandria,_Virginia "Alexandria, Virginia") to help with search and rescue operations.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-NBC-55)

Fireboats and divers were deployed to search for victims and survivors; cold temperatures, strong winds, ice, and murky water hampered rescue efforts. The water temperature near the crash site was recorded at 35°F (2°C). On January 30, the rescue operation turned into a recovery mission.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-56) By February 4, all bodies had been recovered, including the three soldiers in the helicopter, and all of them were identified by February 5.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-VPM_2025-25)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-57)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-58)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-59)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-60) After the collision, Reagan National Airport suspended all takeoffs and landings, diverting flights to nearby airports, including [Dulles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport "Dulles International Airport"), [Baltimore/Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore/Washington_International_Airport "Baltimore/Washington International Airport"),[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-61) and [Richmond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richmond_International_Airport "Richmond International Airport").[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-62) The [Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Metropolitan_Area_Transit_Authority "Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority") extended [Silver Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_Line_(Washington_Metro) "Silver Line (Washington Metro)") service to help passengers whose flights were diverted to Dulles and dispatched "warming buses" to help relief operations.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-63)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-NBC-55) The airport remained closed for over fourteen hours, until 11:00 a.m. on January 30.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-64)

The [fuselage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuselage "Fuselage") of Flight 5342 was found upside down in three sections in the river and was recovered.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-Regan-2025-5) The search for debris was extended to the [Woodrow Wilson Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodrow_Wilson_Bridge "Woodrow Wilson Bridge"), three miles (5 km) south of the airport.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-AP-3) A crane used to lift debris after the March 2024 [collapse of the Francis Scott Key Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Scott_Key_Bridge_collapse "Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse") in Baltimore was brought to help pick up plane wreckage,[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-65) and the [US Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy "United States Navy") also sent two barges to recover heavy items.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-66) According to federal officials, the wreckage of the helicopter was also recovered and was transported to a secure location.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-67)

### Figure skating community

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Figure skating community")]

Among the passengers on the jet were 28 [U.S. Figure Skating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Figure_Skating "U.S. Figure Skating") athletes, coaches, and family members returning from a national development camp held in conjunction with the [2025 U.S. Figure Skating Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_U.S._Figure_Skating_Championships "2025 U.S. Figure Skating Championships") in Wichita, Kansas. This included eleven skaters, all between the ages of 11 and 16, as well as thirteen accompanying parents and four coaches.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-GS013025-68)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-69)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-70)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-71)

Due to the low number of any other direct passenger flights between Wichita and the East Coast, Flight 5342 was the most direct route home for many visitors from the [Northeast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northeastern_United_States "Northeastern United States").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-Draper-18) Most of the athlete victims were too young to be viable candidates for the [2026 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Winter_Olympics "2026 Winter Olympics") but would have been eligible for the [2030 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2030_Winter_Olympics "2030 Winter Olympics").[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-Schleicher-72)

The four coaches killed were all former Soviet/Russian figure skaters. This included married couple [Evgenia Shishkova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evgenia_Shishkova "Evgenia Shishkova") and [Vadim Naumov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vadim_Naumov "Vadim Naumov"), who had won gold medals in [pair skating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pair_skating "Pair skating") at the [1994 World Figure Skating Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_World_Figure_Skating_Championships "1994 World Figure Skating Championships"),[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-73) as well as [Inna Volyanskaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inna_Volyanskaya "Inna Volyanskaya") and [Alexandr Kirsanov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandr_Kirsanov "Alexandr Kirsanov"), who had competed in pairs and [ice dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice_dancer "Ice dancer"), respectively.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-74)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-75)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-76)

On March 2, 2025, [Maxim Naumov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxim_Naumov "Maxim Naumov"), the son of Shishkova and Naumov, performed alongside other notable figure skaters and family members of victims at _[Legacy on Ice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legacy\_on\_Ice "Legacy on Ice"),_ a two-hour tribute show held at Washington, D.C.'s [Capital One Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_One_Arena "Capital One Arena") in honor of the victims of the collision. The impact of the crash on U.S. Figure Skating is similar to that of [Sabena Flight 548](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabena_Flight_548 "Sabena Flight 548"), which killed the entire 1961 U.S. Figure Skating team, most of whom were from the Skating Club of Boston. The [Skating Club of Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skating_Club_of_Boston "Skating Club of Boston") lost six club members in the crash of Flight 5342.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-GS013025-68)

On January 31, 2025, the FAA restricted helicopter flights near the airport. The FAA partially closed both the route that the Black Hawk was on when it collided with the CRJ700 and another route that runs south of the [Key Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Key_Bridge_(Washington,_D.C.) "Key Bridge (Washington, D.C.)") in Washington and connects the neighborhood of [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_(Washington,_D.C.) "Georgetown (Washington, D.C.)") to [Rosslyn, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosslyn,_Virginia "Rosslyn, Virginia"). Separately, two staff members of the Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority were taken into custody on suspicion of providing [CNN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN "CNN") with surveillance footage of the crash.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-86)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-87)

A "memorial bench" was built in [Alexandria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandria,_Virginia "Alexandria, Virginia") on the side of the Potomac River near to where the two aircraft crashed, which is inscribed with the words "May the 67 lives lost over these waters on January 29, 2025 be forever remembered."[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-88)

## Investigation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Investigation")]

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/PSA_Airlines_Flight_5342_wreckage_with_skyline_and_runway_for_bearings.png/250px-PSA_Airlines_Flight_5342_wreckage_with_skyline_and_runway_for_bearings.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PSA_Airlines_Flight_5342_wreckage_with_skyline_and_runway_for_bearings.png)

Remains of the wreckage with the skyline in the background

The [National Transportation Safety Board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Transportation_Safety_Board "National Transportation Safety Board") (NTSB), the FAA, the [US Department of Defense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Defense "United States Department of Defense"), and the US Army announced they would launch investigations into the collision.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-AP-3) The NTSB prepared an investigation team to send to the accident site.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-NBC-55) To retain needed personnel after the crash, the agency acquired an exemption from the ["Fork in the Road" memo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fork_in_the_Road_(Office_of_Personnel_Management_memo) "Fork in the Road (Office of Personnel Management memo)") which purported to allow all of its agents to quit with severance paid through September 2025.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-89) The [Federal Bureau of Investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation "Federal Bureau of Investigation") (FBI) also stated it would help with the response. However, there were no indications of terrorism or criminal activity.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-NBC-55) The [Transportation Safety Board of Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transportation_Safety_Board_of_Canada "Transportation Safety Board of Canada") (TSB) deployed two investigators to help the investigation, since the Bombardier CRJ700 was designed and manufactured in Canada.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-90)

On the evening of January 30, the [flight recorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flight_recorder "Flight recorder") ("black box") of Flight 5342 was recovered from the wreckage and brought to the NTSB lab for evaluation.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-ABC_News:_Black_boxes-91)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-92) The helicopter's flight recorder was recovered on January 31.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-BBC-2025-93)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-ABC_News:_Black_boxes-91)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-94)

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e5/NTSB_recovery_of_crash_related_items_on_the_Potomac_River%2C_2_February_2025_-_2.jpg/250px-NTSB_recovery_of_crash_related_items_on_the_Potomac_River%2C_2_February_2025_-_2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:NTSB_recovery_of_crash_related_items_on_the_Potomac_River,_2_February_2025_-_2.jpg)

NTSB investigators recovering pieces of wreckage from the Potomac River on February 2

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e5/Flight_data_recorder_from_NTSB_recovery_of_crash_related_items_on_the_Potomac_River%2C_2_February_2025_-_1_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Flight_data_recorder_from_NTSB_recovery_of_crash_related_items_on_the_Potomac_River%2C_2_February_2025_-_1_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Flight_data_recorder_from_NTSB_recovery_of_crash_related_items_on_the_Potomac_River,_2_February_2025_-_1_(cropped).jpg)

Flight recorder of the UH-60 Black Hawk helicopter recovered by the NTSB from the Potomac River on February 2

According to the NTSB, at the moment of impact, the helicopter was at a radio altitude of 278 feet (85 m).[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-NTSB2025-02-14-21) Reagan National requires helicopters on that route to stay at or below 200 feet (61 m) above mean sea level.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-Bowman_2025-95) The altitude that the [barometric altimeter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pressure_altimeter "Pressure altimeter") displayed to the helicopter crew was not recorded by the flight recorder. Investigators would normally calculate the barometric altitude displayed to the crew using [pressure altitude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pressure_altitude "Pressure altitude") recorded by the flight recorder, but investigators determined that the data was not valid.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-NTSB2025-02-14-21)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-NPRAltimeter-96)

Senators [Ted Cruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Cruz "Ted Cruz") and [Tammy Duckworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tammy_Duckworth "Tammy Duckworth") addressed questions about the automatic dependent surveillance-broadcast system ([ADS-B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ADS-B "ADS-B")) which was reportedly turned off on the Black Hawk. Some flight data was being sent from the aircraft but the safety system sends what is considered the most-accurate data.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-97) The NTSB confirmed ADS-B was not broadcasting from the helicopter and said they would investigate if there was an equipment malfunction or it was turned off.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-98)

A single [air traffic controller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_traffic_controller "Air traffic controller") was managing both aircraft at the time of the crash, an arrangement deemed "not normal" for that time of day at the airport.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-Ember_2025-36) According to the helicopter's cockpit voice and data recorder, the helicopter crew may have missed parts of two transmissions made by the air traffic controller regarding the jet. Two minutes before the collision, the part of the transmission which said that the plane was "circling" to runway 33 was not heard on the recording. Seventeen seconds before the crash, the part of the transmission stating "pass behind the" was interrupted by the helicopter crew keying their mic to communicate with the air traffic controller.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-NTSB2025-02-14-21)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-NPRAltimeter-96)

About nineteen seconds before impact, the crew of Flight 5342 received an automated [traffic advisory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traffic_collision_avoidance_system#Types_of_traffic_and_resolution_advisories "Traffic collision avoidance system") alert from the [TCAS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traffic_collision_avoidance_system "Traffic collision avoidance system") system. Data from the flight recorder showed the PSA jet [pitched](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_principal_axes "Aircraft principal axes") up about one second before impact, but investigators did not say whether this was an attempted evasive maneuver by the PSA pilots.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-99)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-Peluffo_2025-38)

### NTSB preliminary report and recommendations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: NTSB preliminary report and recommendations")]

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/13/NTSB_Runway_33_-_Helicopter_4_Proximity.jpg/250px-NTSB_Runway_33_-_Helicopter_4_Proximity.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:NTSB_Runway_33_-_Helicopter_4_Proximity.jpg)

NTSB diagram showing proximity between the two routes

The NTSB released a preliminary report on March 11, 2025, accompanied by two urgent safety recommendations to the FAA regarding flight traffic decongestion. Investigators reviewed years of encounters between helicopters and commercial aircraft near Reagan National Airport, finding that "at least one [traffic collision avoidance system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traffic_collision_avoidance_system "Traffic collision avoidance system") (TCAS) resolution advisory was triggered per month" since 2011.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-NTSB_Preliminary_Report-10):18

Helicopters flying within the route 4 corridor, which is designated for operations "at or below 200 feet (61 m)," would have only 75 feet (23 m) of vertical separation from a plane landing on runway 33 if flying directly over the eastern shoreline of the Potomac River.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-Homendy75Feet-100) Since route 4 lacks lateral boundaries or instructions to operate a defined distance from the shoreline, this already minimal separation decreases further when a helicopter operates farther from the shore. This vertical separation also decreases if an airplane is operating below the 3° visual glidepath provided by runway 33's [precision approach path indicator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Precision_approach_path_indicator "Precision approach path indicator") (PAPI). The board concluded that the proximity of route 4 to runway 33's approach path posed "an intolerable risk to aviation safety."[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-NTSB_Recommendations-1)

The NTSB urgently recommended that the FAA close route 4 near the airport during runway 33 landings or opposite-direction takeoffs and designate an alternate helicopter route during those times.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-NTSB_Recommendations-1)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-101) NTSB Chair [Jennifer Homendy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Homendy "Jennifer Homendy") expressed anger that the FAA had not used the same near-miss data her investigators relied on to identify the risk and examine the helicopter routes before the crash occurred and said, "It does make me angry, but it also makes me feel incredibly devastated for families that are grieving."[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-102) The near-miss data from October 2021 to December 2024 highlighted 15,214 close-proximity events between helicopters and commercial planes, including 85 incidents that were dangerously separated less than 1,500 feet horizontally and 200 feet vertically.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-WJLAProximity-103)

### Findings and recommendations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Findings and recommendations")]

The NTSB held a three-day investigative hearing from July 30 to August 1, 2025, and a public meeting on this investigation on January 27, 2026.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-NTSB_Investigation-104) It published 74 findings and 50 recommendations to prevent similar accidents in the future.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-NTSB_Press_Release_2026-105)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-AIR-26-02_Final_Report-7)

The probable cause of the accident, according to the NTSB, was the placement of a helicopter route in close proximity to a runway approach path by the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA). The FAA did not regularly evaluate route safety data and did not implement recommendations proposed to reduce risk of midair collision near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport. Also, the air traffic system was overreliant on visual separation for efficiency, discarding the inherent limitations of this "see-and-avoid" concept, and the helicopter crew did not apply visual separation, causing the collision.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-NTSB_Investigation-104)

Significant additional factors included:[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-NTSB_Investigation-104)

*   Air traffic control tower team's loss of situation awareness and degraded performance due to the high workload of the combined helicopter and local control positions. The absence of a risk assessment process to identify and mitigate real-time operational risk factors, which resulted in misprioritization of duties, inadequate traffic advisories, and the lack of safety alerts to both flight crews;
*   The failure of the US Army to ensure pilots' awareness of the effects of error tolerances on barometric altimeters in their helicopters, which resulted in the crew flying above the maximum published helicopter route altitude.

## Lawsuit

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Lawsuit")]

On February 18, 2025, on behalf of one of the victims of Flight 5342, attorney [Robert A. Clifford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_A._Clifford "Robert A. Clifford") filed a $250 million tort complaint against the Federal Aviation Administration and the US Army under the [Federal Tort Claims Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Tort_Claims_Act "Federal Tort Claims Act") under Form 95. The government had six months to respond and act on the claim; if the government allowed the deadline to expire, the plaintiff would have the right to sue in federal district court.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-106) Attorney Clifford sued on September 24 in federal court in D.C., alleging criminal negligence. Defendants were PSA Airlines, American Airlines, the US Army, and the federal government. At a press conference, Clifford said passenger Casey Crafton died as a result of systematic failings and a careless disregard for safety.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-107) More families were added to the Clifford case. Clifford partnered with the [Kreindler & Kreindler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kreindler_&_Kreindler "Kreindler & Kreindler") law firm in New York City. The US Army said it would not comment. American Airlines denied responsibility.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-108) On December 17, the government admitted in a court filing in response to the lawsuit that it was partially at fault for the crash and that it owed and had breached its [duty of care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duty_of_care "Duty of care") to the plaintiffs. The filing said that an air traffic controller did not follow the proper procedure for visual separation and that the helicopter pilots failed to remain vigilant. The airline has filed motions to dismiss the claims against them.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-109)

On July 30, attorney Robert Curtis filed another federal tort complaint for $200 million on behalf of another victim of Flight 5342, setting a separate six-month deadline for the government to respond.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-110)

"We are not going to litigate this case in the press", Judge Reyes warned, adding that while defendants may make public remarks when submitting their answers, they must abstain from further debate. Robert's comment was revealed after the federal government acknowledged some culpability, which infuriated Reyes, who warned that future disobedience of court orders could result in consequences. The complaints are consolidated before Reyes, and on February 27, there will be a hearing on petitions to dismiss; by that time, the judge will have declined American Airlines's request to dismiss from this lawsuit. American Airlines contends that the plaintiff attorneys have not shown that they have broken any federal rules or regulations.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-111)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-112)

Another lawsuit was filed against the federal government and American Airlines from the [Jacksonville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville,_Florida "Jacksonville, Florida")-based Spohrer Dodd law firm on behalf of another victim, and they said 60 lawsuits were filed in federal courts.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-113)

## Responses

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Responses")]

### Aviation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Aviation")]

American Airlines CEO [Robert Isom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Isom "Robert Isom"), in a video statement produced by the airline, expressed that he was "absolutely heartbroken".[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-AAPReleases-114) He went on to state that AA "[didn't] know why the military aircraft came into the path" but that he pledged full cooperation with federal investigators. American Airlines also activated a "care team" for family members of passengers on Flight 5342, including a hotline allowing families to find out if their family members were on board.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-Regan-2025-5)

[Chesley "Sully" Sullenberger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sully_Sullenberger "Sully Sullenberger"), an aviation safety expert and the pilot of [US Airways Flight 1549](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Airways_Flight_1549 "US Airways Flight 1549") that ditched in the [Hudson River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hudson_River "Hudson River") in 2009, argued for more safety zones and restrictions on flight patterns.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-Regan-2025-5)

### Domestic

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Domestic")]

President [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") was briefed within an hour after the 8:47pm collision. Shortly after midnight, he wrote on [Truth Social](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Truth_Social "Truth Social") questioning the actions of the air traffic controllers and asserting that the situation could have been prevented.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-CNBC_Trump_lashes-115) He also criticized the helicopter crew for flying too high.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-116) Later that morning, Trump released a statement calling the crash a "terrible accident," thanking emergency responders and saying of the victims: "May God bless their souls."[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-Knox-Jan30-117)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-NBC-55)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-Regan-2025-5)

Trump alleged that the FAA's [diversity, equity, and inclusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diversity,_equity,_and_inclusion "Diversity, equity, and inclusion") (DEI) goals supported by former presidents [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden") and [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") may have been partly to blame for the crash by stating "they actually came out with a directive, too White."[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-CNBC_Trump_lashes-115)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-Sanger_2025-118) Thrown into the light was a policy introduced in 2013 by the Obama administration's FAA that encouraged the hiring of minorities as air traffic controllers. This policy was continued by the first Trump administration's FAA.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-119)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-120) He harshly criticized former transportation secretary [Pete Buttigieg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_Buttigieg "Pete Buttigieg"), accusing him of prioritizing diversity in the FAA.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-Sanger_2025-118)

Trump criticized the FAA for targeting disabilities such as "hearing, vision, missing extremities, partial or complete paralysis, [epilepsy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epilepsy "Epilepsy"), severe [intellectual disability](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intellectual_disability "Intellectual disability"), psychiatric disability and [dwarfism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwarfism "Dwarfism")" for special emphasis in recruitment and hiring. This was a policy introduced in 2019 by his own first administration's FAA, which announced a program to allow 20 people with "targeted disabilities" to train at air traffic control centers for air traffic operations careers. Several disabilities such as epilepsy, [poor vision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poor_vision "Poor vision"), and some [mental disorders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mental_disorder "Mental disorder") were still disqualifying for air traffic controller positions per FAA and [OPM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Office_of_Personnel_Management "United States Office of Personnel Management") regulations.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-121)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-122)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-123)

Trump said that he would meet with families of the victims, but rebuffed the idea of visiting the site of the accident after being pressed by reporters during a briefing, asking, "What's the site? The water? You want me to go swimming?"[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-124)

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/08/Coast_Guard_responds_to_aviation_incident_in_the_Potomac_River_%288848276%29.jpg/250px-Coast_Guard_responds_to_aviation_incident_in_the_Potomac_River_%288848276%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Coast_Guard_responds_to_aviation_incident_in_the_Potomac_River_(8848276).jpg)

[Coast Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Coast_Guard "United States Coast Guard") response teams at the scene on January 30

Trump received pushback and criticism for his claims that DEI initiatives were to blame for the crash, including by Buttigieg, who said that Trump's claims were "despicable" and that he should be "leading, not lying".[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-125) Representative [Ilhan Omar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilhan_Omar "Ilhan Omar") of Minnesota criticized Trump for "blaming this deadly crash on minorities and white women" and that the comments were "disgusting, racist and sexist".[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-CNBC_Trump_lashes-115)[Senate Minority Leader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_Minority_Leader "Senate Minority Leader")[Chuck Schumer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Schumer "Chuck Schumer") of New York also criticized Trump's remarks, calling them "idle speculation". Maryland Senator [Chris Van Hollen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Van_Hollen "Chris Van Hollen") criticized Trump by stating that he was "making a political show out of this awful tragedy" about the crash.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-BBC-47) Senator [Chris Murphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Murphy "Chris Murphy") of Connecticut stated that Trump was "blaming Black people and blaming women who work at the FAA without any evidence."[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-Sangal_2025-83) Representative [Jesús "Chuy" García](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuy_Garc%C3%ADa "Chuy García") of Illinois stated that Trump was "exploiting disaster to continue to spread racist lies and divisiveness across the country."[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-Sangal_2025-83)[Sully Sullenberger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sully_Sullenberger "Sully Sullenberger") responded to Trump by stating that "an airplane cannot know or care" about a pilot's race or gender but can only care about "what control inputs are made" and that he was "disgusted" by Trump's comments.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-126)

Meanwhile, Trump administration officials agreed with his claim that such policies may have caused the crash.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-Megerian-127)[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-Saric-128) Vice President [JD Vance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JD_Vance "JD Vance") said, "When you don't have the best standards in who you're hiring, it means on the one hand, you're not getting the best people in government. But on the other hand, it puts stresses on the people who are already there."[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-Megerian-127)[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-129)[Sean Duffy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Duffy "Sean Duffy"), the transportation secretary, said, "We can only accept the best and the brightest in positions of safety," while [Pete Hegseth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_Hegseth "Pete Hegseth"), the [United States Secretary of Defense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Defense "United States Secretary of Defense"), said, "The era of DEI is gone at the Defense Department and we need the best and brightest," including in "our air traffic control."[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-Saric-128) Duffy also said, "What I've seen so far, do I think this was preventable? Absolutely."[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-130) Hegseth also said that the helicopter crew was "fairly experienced," and undergoing "routine annual retraining—night flights on a standard [flight] corridor for a [continuity-of-government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continuity_of_government "Continuity of government") mission."[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-131) White House Press Secretary [Karoline Leavitt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karoline_Leavitt "Karoline Leavitt") supported Trump's claim by stating that it was "common sense" to be concerned about potential negative effects of DEI initiatives.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-BBC-47)

Duffy publicly blamed diversity and social justice, "when you don't focus on safety and you focus on social justice or the environment, bad things happen." He criticized the Biden administration and former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg for changing terms like "cockpit" to the more gender-neutral "flight deck" and "Notice to Airmen" to "Notice to Air Mission," suggesting changes to terminology made aviation less safe.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-132) Duffy denied the current [federal hiring freeze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_United_States_federal_hiring_freeze "2025 United States federal hiring freeze") and buy-out scheme implemented by the Trump administration played any role in the FAA staff shortages of air traffic controllers.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-133)

### International

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: International")]

The [International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") extended "heartfelt sympathies to all those affected, which we understand may include Olympians, young athletes, and their support staff."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-Regan-2025-5) At the [2025 European Figure Skating Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_European_Figure_Skating_Championships "2025 European Figure Skating Championships"), which had begun the morning of the collision, a moment of silence was observed to mourn the figure skaters and family members lost. The [International Skating Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Skating_Union "International Skating Union") and many international skating federations also offered condolences.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-134)

[Pope Francis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Francis "Pope Francis") sent a [telegram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telegram_of_condolence "Telegram of condolence") to the White House expressing condolences for the victims of the collision.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-135)[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-136) The [Russian Embassy in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embassy_of_Russia,_Washington,_D.C. "Embassy of Russia, Washington, D.C.") sent condolences to the families of the Russian nationals who died in the crash.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-BBC-47) The [Chinese foreign ministry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Foreign_Affairs_(China) "Ministry of Foreign Affairs (China)") expressed condolences to the families of the crash victims and demanded a full investigation of the disaster.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-china-78) Canadian Prime Minister [Justin Trudeau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Trudeau "Justin Trudeau") offered his condolences "to the grieving family members and loved ones who are facing unimaginable loss."[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Potomac_River_mid-air_collision#cite_note-137)

# FAA Statements on Aviation Accidents and Incidents

The information below is preliminary and subject to change. News media with questions on other topics may contact us at [pressoffice@faa.gov](mailto:pressoffice@faa.gov).

**For General Aviation:**

•Contact local authorities for the names and medical conditions of anyone on board.   
•A [preliminary FAA report will be posted](https://www.faa.gov/data_research/accident_incident/preliminary_data), usually on the next business day.  
•If known, the aircraft registration number (N-number) can be searched at the [Aircraft Registry](http://registry.faa.gov/aircraftinquiry/Search/NNumberInquiry).  
•If the National Transportation Safety Board ([NTSB](https://www.ntsb.gov/news/Pages/media_resources.aspx)) is also investigating, it will provide all updates.

**For Commercial Aviation:**

•Contact the airline for information about passengers and crew, flights and schedules.  
•If the National Transportation Safety Board is also investigating, it will provide all updates.

### September 15, 2026

**General Aviation / Chatsworth, California**

# FAA Statements on Aviation Accidents and Incidents

The information below is preliminary and subject to change. News media with questions on other topics may contact us at [pressoffice@faa.gov](mailto:pressoffice@faa.gov).

**For General Aviation:**

•Contact local authorities for the names and medical conditions of anyone on board.   
•A [preliminary FAA report will be posted](https://www.faa.gov/data_research/accident_incident/preliminary_data), usually on the next business day.  
•If known, the aircraft registration number (N-number) can be searched at the [Aircraft Registry](http://registry.faa.gov/aircraftinquiry/Search/NNumberInquiry).  
•If the National Transportation Safety Board ([NTSB](https://www.ntsb.gov/news/Pages/media_resources.aspx)) is also investigating, it will provide all updates.

**For Commercial Aviation:**

•Contact the airline for information about passengers and crew, flights and schedules.  
•If the National Transportation Safety Board is also investigating, it will provide all updates.

# UPS Flight 2976 Crash During Takeoff

## What Happened

What Happened

​_This information is preliminary and subject to change.​​_​

Updated 1/14/2026

On November 4, 2025, about 1714 eastern standard time (EST), United Parcel Service (UPS) flight 2976, a Boeing (McDonnell-Douglas) MD-11F airplane, N259UP, was destroyed after it impacted the ground shortly after takeoff from runway 17R at Louisville Muhammad Ali International Airport (SDF), Louisville, Kentucky. The 3 crewmembers aboard the airplane and 11 people on the ground were fatally injured. There were 23 others on the ground who were injured. Flight 2976 was a domestic cargo flight operating under the provisions of Title 14 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 121 from SDF to Daniel K. Inouye International Airport (HNL), Honolulu, Hawaii.

​In response to the accident, the NTSB traveled to SDF on November 5, 2025, and started the process of documenting the accident site, and collecting the perishable data necessary for the investigation.

As part of the investigative process, the NTSB invited qualified parties to participate in the investigation. These included:

*   the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA),
*   UPS,
*   The Boeing Company,
*   Independent Pilots Association (IPA),  
*   General Electric (GE) Aerospace, 
*   Teamsters Airline Division.​ and
*   ​​Collins Aerospace

# UPS Flight 2976 Crash During Takeoff

## What Happened

What Happened

​_This information is preliminary and subject to change.​​_​

Updated 1/14/2026

On November 4, 2025, about 1714 eastern standard time (EST), United Parcel Service (UPS) flight 2976, a Boeing (McDonnell-Douglas) MD-11F airplane, N259UP, was destroyed after it impacted the ground shortly after takeoff from runway 17R at Louisville Muhammad Ali International Airport (SDF), Louisville, Kentucky. The 3 crewmembers aboard the airplane and 11 people on the ground were fatally injured. There were 23 others on the ground who were injured. Flight 2976 was a domestic cargo flight operating under the provisions of Title 14 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 121 from SDF to Daniel K. Inouye International Airport (HNL), Honolulu, Hawaii.

​In response to the accident, the NTSB traveled to SDF on November 5, 2025, and started the process of documenting the accident site, and collecting the perishable data necessary for the investigation.

As part of the investigative process, the NTSB invited qualified parties to participate in the investigation. These included:

*   the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA),
*   UPS,
*   The Boeing Company,
*   Independent Pilots Association (IPA),  
*   General Electric (GE) Aerospace, 
*   Teamsters Airline Division.​ and
*   ​​Collins Aerospace

# Aviation Investigation Final Report              

> Location: Augusta, Georgia Accident Number: ERA24FA206
> Date & Time: May 2, 2024, 07:13 Local Registration: N629BE
> Aircraft: RAYTHEON AIRCRAFT COMPANY A36 Aircraft Damage: Destroyed
> Defining Event: Aerodynamic stall/spin Injuries: 1 Fatal
> Flight Conducted Under: Part 91: General aviation - Personal

## Analysis 

Shortly after takeoff on a cross-country flight in day visual meteorological conditions, the pilot initiated a sharp turn to the left with the landing gear extended and the flaps retracted. The turn appeared roughly consistent with an attempt to return to the airport; however, no distress calls were noted and the airport did not record the common traffic advisory frequency. The airplane reached a maximum altitude of 300 feet above the ground and a maximum calibrated airspeed of 90 kts. The airplane turned at more than twice the standard rate, reaching a calculated bank angle of 44° left wing low before it appeared to enter an accelerated aerodynamic stall. Sound spectrum analysis of surveillance video revealed the propeller was running at near maximum rpm at impact. The airplane impacted the ground in a residential neighborhood, was destroyed in a postaccident fire. A postaccident examination of the airframe and engine revealed no evidence of a preexisting malfunction or failure. The reason for the pilot’s apparent return to the airport after departure could not be determined. 

## Probable Cause and Findings 

The National Transportation Safety Board determines the probable cause(s) of this accident to be: 

The pilot’s excessive turn rate and bank angle while at low airspeed and altitude, resulting in an accelerated aerodynamic stall, loss of airplane control, and collision with terrain. Page 2 of 9 ERA24FA206 

Findings 

Aircraft  Angle of attack - Capability exceeded 

Personnel issues  Aircraft control - Pilot Page 3 of 9 ERA24FA206 

## Factual Information 

History of Flight   

> Initial climb Aerodynamic stall/spin (Defining event)
> Uncontrolled descent Collision with terr/obj (non-CFIT)

# Aviation Investigation Final Report              

> Location: Boston, Massachusetts Accident Number: ERA24LA386
> Date & Time: September 17, 2024, 17:30 Local Registration: N18VV
> Aircraft: Cessna 402 Aircraft Damage: Substantial
> Defining Event: Sys/Comp malf/fail (non-power) Injuries: 3 None
> Flight Conducted Under: Part 135: Air taxi & commuter - Scheduled

## Analysis 

The pilot reported that during climb out, he noticed a flicker of both the left and right hydraulic flow lights. He thought the airplane was losing hydraulic pressure, so he tried to extend the landing gear before all pressure was lost. Only the left main landing gear position green light illuminated. The hydraulic flow lights then illuminated steadily. He returned to the airport and performed the emergency landing gear extension checklist; however, the right and nose landing gear did not extend, and he landed with only the left main landing gear extended. 

A postaccident examination of the airplane revealed that a solid hydraulic line connected to the hydraulic filter was fractured and the system contained no hydraulic fluid. It is likely that the fracture of the hydraulic line and the subsequent loss of hydraulic fluid resulted in the partial landing gear extension. A review of the airplane’s maintenance records could not determine the age of the hydraulic line or if any maintenance had been performed on the hydraulic line. Postaccident testing of the emergency landing gear extension system revealed that if functioned normally when the activation handle was fully extended. Based on this information, it is likely the pilot did not pull the emergency handle out far enough to activate the system. 

## Probable Cause and Findings 

The National Transportation Safety Board determines the probable cause(s) of this accident to be: Page 2 of 6 ERA24LA386 

The failure of a solid hydraulic fluid line, which resulted in a loss of hydraulic fluid that prevented the landing gear extension process from completing normally. Contributing to the outcome was the pilot’s failure to fully activate the emergency landing gear extension system. 

Findings     

> Aircraft Gear extension and retract sys - Failure
> Personnel issues Use of equip/system - Pilot
> Aircraft Gear extension and retract sys - Incorrect use/operation Page 3 of 6 ERA24LA386

## Factual Information 

History of Flight    

> Initial climb Sys/Comp malf/fail (non-power) (Defining event)
> Emergency descent Landing gear not configured
> Landing Abnormal runway contact

On September 17, 2024, about 1730 eastern daylight time, a Cessna 402C, N18VV, was substantially damaged when it was involved in an accident near Boston, Massachusetts. The pilot and two passengers were not injured. The airplane was operated by Cape Air as a Title 14 

Code of Federal Regulations Part 135 scheduled passenger flight. 

According to the pilot, during climb out, he noticed a flicker of both the left and right hydraulic flow lights. He thought the airplane was losing hydraulic pressure, so he tried to extend the landing gear before all pressure was lost. Only the left main landing gear position green light illuminated. The hydraulic flow lights then illuminated steadily. He made the decision to return to the departure airport, notified air traffic control of the situation, and asked for delaying radar vectors to the airport in order to run the checklists. The pilot then followed the "Landing Gear Will Not Extend Hydraulically" checklist. He noted that the landing gear position indicating lights were working when he checked the “press to test,” just as they were on the ground before takeoff. He slowed the airplane to under 130 knots with the landing gear switch already in the down position. He then pulled the “GEAR HYD” circuit breaker and pulled the emergency landing gear extension handle. There was no change of position indicator lights or any indication/noise that the landing gear had extended. 

He subsequently landed on the left main landing gear and began lowering the airplane’s nose. During the landing roll, the airplane’s right wing contacted a runway light, after which it started to leak fuel. The airplane came to rest upright on the right side of the runway, at an intersection of the runway and taxiway. 

Further examination of the airplane’s hydraulic system by the operator’s maintenance department revealed that a solid hydraulic line connected to the hydraulic system filter was fractured, and that all of the hydraulic fluid had drained out of the system. The maintenance personnel performed the emergency landing gear extension procedure by pulling the landing gear emergency extension handle all the way out and observed all three landing gear come down and lock. 

A review of the airplane’s maintenance records could not determine the age of the hydraulic line or if any maintenance had been performed on the hydraulic line. Page 4 of 6 ERA24LA386 

Following the accident, the operator issued a Technical Notice to all maintenance personnel to stress the importance of general inspection criteria while performing maintenance on the airplanes.

# Aviation Investigation Classification

Page Content

​​​The NTSB investigates all civil aviation accidents and select incidents to:

*   Determine the facts, conditions, and circumstances relating to an accident; 
*   Determine one or more probable causes; and 
*   Issue safety recommendations to prevent or mitigate the effects of a similar accident. (See 49 CFR 831.4.)​  

​We begin by assessing available facts to determine the appropriate investigative response. Following an initial assessment, our investigators determine the level of response and work with those who may be affected by, involved in, or have pertinent information about the accident or incident. An investigation will result in a report of the facts and the NTSB's analysis and probable cause of the accident or incident. We may also produce other products designed to improve transportation safety such as safety recommendations, safety alerts, or other safety information.

The NTSB's primary focus is to improve safety for the travelling public. We do not conduct investigations for the purpose of determining the rights, liabilities, or blame of any person or entity. The aim of all NTSB investigations is to prevent the recurrence of other accidents and incidents. We carefully consider the level of detail necessary for each investigation with the aim of concentrating resources on investigations that are most likely to enhance aviation safety while still fulfilling our mandate to investigate all civil aviation accidents. Because many accidents have similar causes and may not provide new safety information that would result in further action, investigating these in detail may not be justified given our limited resources. Thus, our investigators do not launch to the scene of every accident, conduct an in-depth investigation, or produce an extensive report for many accidents with known circumstances.

We have a classification system for investigation depth and final report for each event (accident or incident). The initial classification of an investigation is subject to change depending on the safety issues that are identified throughout the course of the investigation.

## Investigation Classes and Description

**Investigation Class****Description**
​Class 1  
  
​Class 1 investigations are reserved for very significant accidents and are likely to involve substantial NTSB and external resources. They generally involve transport category aircraft and commercial operations.*   ​A large team led by an Air Carrier and Space Investigations or General Aviation Investigations division senior investigator-in-charge who conducts the investigation. NTSB subject matter experts form and lead multiple investigative groups to identify and address safety issues. The investigative team will usually travel to and spend considerable time at the scene of the accident and conduct follow-on investigative activities.  

*   Investigation updates or interim reports may be released during the investigation. Following a final technical review of the gathered facts and analysis, a final comprehensive report will be made available to the public. The Board members may deliberate the findings, probable cause, and recommendations accompanying the report at a public “sunshine" meeting.
Class 2  
  
​​​​​Class 2 investigations generally have a broad scope and involve a significant effort collecting evidence across several investigative areas and a substantial investment of resources. These investigations may involve:​​   
> ​​Very complex systems and/or processes,   
> Multiple organizations, or   
​> Poor risk controls implemented by the operator, manufacturer, maintainer, and regulator.*   ​​​​A large team led by an Air Carrier and Space Investigations or General Aviation Investigations division senior investigator-in-charge who conducts the investigation​.
*   Following a technical review of the gathered facts and analysis, a final comprehensive report will be made available to the public​following Board approval that identifies the probable cause(s) of the accident and factors that contributed to the outcome of the accident, if any.   
*   Findings from these investigations may be used to support recommendations, or the investigative team may work with industry stakeholders directly to resolve safety issues identified during the investigation. Accidents that involve recurring safety issues may be accompanied by a safety message that includes practical strategies to avoid future accidents.
Class 3  
  
​Class 3 investigations seek to identify safety issues that reveal underlying cause(s) of the accident.*   ​​The investigation is led by an investigator-in-charge, who may be assisted by other NTSB subject matter experts if the investigation requires an in-depth focus on a specific area. The investigative team may travel to the scene of the accident or to other follow-up activities, or the entirety of the investigation may be conducted remotely.  
*   Following a final technical review of the gathered facts and analysis of those facts, a final report will be made available to the public following Board approval that identifies the probable cause(s)of the accident and factors that contributed to the outcome of the accident, if any.  

*   Findings from these investigations may be used to support recommendations, or the investigative team may work with industry stakeholders directly to resolve safety issues identified during the investigation. Accidents that involve recurring safety issues may be accompanied by a safety message that includes practical strategies to avoid future accidents.
Class 4​  
  
​Class 4 investigations seek to identify the cause of the accident.*   ​​An investigator-in-charge leads the investigation. In some cases,the investigator-in-charge may travel to the scene of the accident, but class 4 investigations are generally all conducted remotely.
*   Class 4 investigations are limited in scope and of the shortest duration.A final report will be made available to the public that identifies probable cause(s) following Board approval and within 6 months. The report only examines the actions and conditions directly relating to the accident, and the documented sequence of events and probable cause reached is simple and straightforward.  
*   The investigator-in-charge may work with industry stakeholders to develop solutions to safety issues identified during the investigation. Investigations that involve well known circumstances may be accompanied by a safety message that includes practical strategies to avoid potential future recurrence.​

Following an initial assessment, our investigators determine the level of response and work with those who may be affected by, involved in, or have pertinent information about the accident or incident. An investigation will result in a report of the facts and the NTSB's analysis and probable cause of the accident or incident. We may also produce other products designed to improve transportation safety such as safety recommendations, safety alerts, or other safety information.

The NTSB's primary focus is to improve safety for the travelling public. We do not conduct investigations for the purpose of determining the rights, liabilities, or blame of any person or entity. The aim of all NTSB investigations is to prevent the recurrence of other accidents and incidents. We carefully consider the level of detail necessary for each investigation with the aim of concentrating resources on investigations that are most likely to enhance aviation safety while still fulfilling our mandate to investigate all civil aviation accidents. Because many accidents have similar causes and may not provide new safety information that would result in further action, investigating these in detail may not be justified given our limited resources. Thus, our investigators do not launch to the scene of every accident, conduct an in-depth investigation, or produce an extensive report for many accidents with known circumstances.

We have a classification system for investigation depth and final report for each event (accident or incident). The initial classification of an investigation is subject to change depending on the safety issues that are identified throughout the course of the investigation.

## Investigation Classes and Description

**Investigation Class****Description**
​Class 1  
  
​Class 1 investigations are reserved for very significant accidents and are likely to involve substantial NTSB and external resources. They generally involve transport category aircraft and commercial operations.*   ​A large team led by an Air Carrier and Space Investigations or General Aviation Investigations division senior investigator-in-charge who conducts the investigation. NTSB subject matter experts form and lead multiple investigative groups to identify and address safety issues. The investigative team will usually travel to and spend considerable time at the scene of the accident and conduct follow-on investigative activities.  

*   Investigation updates or interim reports may be released during the investigation. Following a final technical review of the gathered facts and analysis, a final comprehensive report will be made available to the public. The Board members may deliberate the findings, probable cause, and recommendations accompanying the report at a public “sunshine" meeting.
Class 2  
  
​​​​​Class 2 investigations generally have a broad scope and involve a significant effort collecting evidence across several investigative areas and a substantial investment of resources. These investigations may involve:​​   
> ​​Very complex systems and/or processes,   
> Multiple organizations, or   
​> Poor risk controls implemented by the operator, manufacturer, maintainer, and regulator.*   ​​​​A large team led by an Air Carrier and Space Investigations or General Aviation Investigations division senior investigator-in-charge who conducts the investigation​.
*   Following a technical review of the gathered facts and analysis, a final comprehensive report will be made available to the public​following Board approval that identifies the probable cause(s) of the accident and factors that contributed to the outcome of the accident, if any.   
*   Findings from these investigations may be used to support recommendations, or the investigative team may work with industry stakeholders directly to resolve safety issues identified during the investigation. Accidents that involve recurring safety issues may be accompanied by a safety message that includes practical strategies to avoid future accidents.
Class 3  
  
​Class 3 investigations seek to identify safety issues that reveal underlying cause(s) of the accident.*   ​​The investigation is led by an investigator-in-charge, who may be assisted by other NTSB subject matter experts if the investigation requires an in-depth focus on a specific area. The investigative team may travel to the scene of the accident or to other follow-up activities, or the entirety of the investigation may be conducted remotely.  
*   Following a final technical review of the gathered facts and analysis of those facts, a final report will be made available to the public following Board approval that identifies the probable cause(s)of the accident and factors that contributed to the outcome of the accident, if any.  

*   Findings from these investigations may be used to support recommendations, or the investigative team may work with industry stakeholders directly to resolve safety issues identified during the investigation. Accidents that involve recurring safety issues may be accompanied by a safety message that includes practical strategies to avoid future accidents.
Class 4​  
  
​Class 4 investigations seek to identify the cause of the accident.*   ​​An investigator-in-charge leads the investigation. In some cases,the investigator-in-charge may travel to the scene of the accident, but class 4 investigations are generally all conducted remotely.
*   Class 4 investigations are limited in scope and of the shortest duration.A final report will be made available to the public that identifies probable cause(s) following Board approval and within 6 months. The report only examines the actions and conditions directly relating to the accident, and the documented sequence of events and probable cause reached is simple and straightforward.  
*   The investigator-in-charge may work with industry stakeholders to develop solutions to safety issues identified during the investigation. Investigations that involve well known circumstances may be accompanied by a safety message that includes practical strategies to avoid potential future recurrence.​

4.  Organizational Risk Management Strategies

The NTSB has long believed that thesafety of commercial aviation can be
improved using  strategies that enableoperators to proactively address in a
nonpunitive way underlying organizational issues before they result in accidents  .One
such process is an SMS, which is the formal, top  -down, organization-wide approach
to managing safety risk and assuring the effectiveness of safety risk controls.  56 SMS
incorporates proactive safety methods for operators to identify hazards, mitigate risk,
and monitor the extent to which they are meeting their objectives.

Further, theeffectiveness of the safety assurance component of SMS can be
enhanced through safety performance monitoring and measurementtools, such as
an FDM  program  . FDM involves the recording and analysis of flight-related data to
provide vital information regarding trends in operational deviations that may
adversely affect safety during flights  . These objective data can help operators
develop mitigations  , such as improvements in training and procedures,  to  address
such deviations before they lead to an accident.  57

SMS for Part 121 operations has been required since 2018, following a long
history of both international and domestic support, including a 2007 NTSB safety
recommendation.  58 In 2016, we issued three recommendations to the FAA regarding
requiring SMS and FDM equipment and programs for Part 135, and, in 2022, we

56 The goal of an SMS is to identify safety hazards, ensure necessary remedial action is
implemented to maintain an acceptable level of safety, provide continuous monitoring and regular
assessment of the safety level achieved, and continuously improve an organization’s overall level of
safety. The four main components of an SMS are 1) safety policy, which establishes senior
management’s commitment to continually improve safety; 2) safety risk management, which
determines the need for new or revised risk controls; 3) safety assurance, which evaluates the
effectiveness of implemented risk control strategies; and 4) safety promotion, which includes training,
communications, and other actions to create a positive safety culture (FAA 2015b).

57 An FDM program typically involves the use of an onboard device that can record various
flight parameters installed on each aircraft in an operator’s fleet. Periodic review of the recorded data
enables an operator to identify operational exceedances, deviations from company procedures, and
other potential safety issues  and then explore—in a nonpunitive way—the reasons why these events
occurred and what can be done to avoid them in the future.

6.  Conclusions

6.1  Findings

1.  The safety of Title14  Code of Federal Regulations Part 135 operations would
be enhanced by the required use of certificated dispatchers, which would allow
for improved quality control over the functions such as preflight weather, fuel,
and route planning; active monitoring of in-flight aircraft position and
conditions along the route of flight; and timely notification of emergency
response organizations if an aircraft becomes overdue.

2.  Requiring joint operational control responsibility between a certificated
dispatcher and a pilot  -in  -command  can  minimize the likelihoodof a
single-point failure that could affect the safety of  Title  14 Code of Federal
Regulations Part 135operation  s.

3.  Manifest and recordkeeping requirements for all aircraft that are operated
under Title  14Code of Federal Regulations  Part 135 would not only help pilots
detect and correct unsafe loading conditions but also provide operators and
inspectors the information needed to support proactive, comprehensive
assessments to identify any related operational risk areas that may influence
improper aircraft loading and mitigate them before an accident occurs  .

4.  The Federal Aviation Administration’s safety management system  final rule  ,
which requires all Title 14Code of Federal Regulations  Part 135 operators to
incorporate formal system safety methods into their internal oversight
programs, will help these operators proactively identify and mitigate risks to
prevent accidents.

5.  For Title  14  Code of Federal Regulations  Part 135operators  of limited size  and
scope for which the hiring of a certificated dispatcher may not be practical  (such
as single-pilot and  single-pilot  -in  -command  operators  ), implementation of  an
appropriately scaled safety management system thatincludes planning tools to
analyze and assess the inherent risks in operations can help in thedevelop  ment
of effective operational control strategies, including methods for ensuring
adequate preflight weather, route, and fuel planning.

6.  Operational flight data monitoringprograms could provide  Title  14Code of
Federal Regulations Part 135 operators with objective information regarding
the manner in which their pilots conduct flights, and a periodic review of such
information could assist operators in detecting and correcting unsafe deviations
from company standard operating procedures.
